findings: The deployed node runs the pre-closeout binary: no serving_bundle block, no build block, so it cannot state which bundle it LOADED as distinct from what its data directory currently says.

Its lexical generation (2026-08-22, promoted 2026-09-01) and its semantic generation (2026-08-17) are DIFFERENT. The fusion parity guard would skip the fallback on that basis, and LOOM_SEMANTIC_FALLBACK is 0 there, so nothing is being mis-served — but this is precisely the split identity the review asked to be made legible.

It reports semantic.ready = true for an artefact whose sidecar declares no embedding model. Under the new contract that same artefact reports ready = false with a named reason. Readiness there currently means 'the database opened and is non-empty', which is the over-promise ADR-137's closeout names.

remaining: HP deployment: the production facade must be redeployed onto this binary before any of the above is production evidence. Not done here by instruction — the running facade was read only.
Corpus publisher: the exporter must stamp embeddingModel (and ideally dimensions) into <artifact>.generation.json, or the deployment must set LOOM_SEMANTIC_REQUIRE_MODEL_ID=0 as a knowing exception.
Mirror: app/mirror.sh still promotes file-at-a-time. loom-facade's BundlePromoter implements the staged, commit-marker-last protocol; porting the shell mirror onto it (or invoking it) is outstanding.
The compose data-directory mismatch (app/data vs the repository data directory) is unchanged documented operational debt.
Recall/benchmark work is untouched: no recall or performance claim is made or verified here.

incidental_observations.observation: git reports the file as modified after the local facade run: same size (34222080 bytes), differing bytes.
incidental_observations.cause: loom-vector-ruvector opens the artefact through ruvector_core::VectorDB::new, which opens the underlying redb database READ/WRITE. Merely opening it rewrites redb transaction metadata even though the adapter never writes a vector.
incidental_observations.significance: This confirms the open question the consumed-vector review raised — 'Verify read-only serving intent against the storage opener's behaviour'. A serving node's semantic read path is not read-only at the filesystem level, which matters for a read-only mount, for a shared artefact, and for any content digest computed over the .rvdb itself. The bundle content digest is unaffected in this deployment because the marker covers the JSON indices.
incidental_observations.action_taken: Left as found. Reverting was outside this task's remit (no checkout/revert), and the modification is a real property of the consumer worth carrying rather than tidying away.
incidental_observations.remediation: Either open the artefact read-only in the adapter (needs a ruvector-core API that does not take a write transaction on open), or exclude the .rvdb from any content digest and treat it as a locally-mutable cache of a published set.
